jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in Minnesota, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in Minnesota, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you.
jsonld.keywords: Minnesota district map, what district am I in, Minnesota Senate district, Minnesota House district, county commissioner district, civic districts, who represents me Minnesota

brand.tagline: Every civic district that covers your point in Minnesota, and who represents you there.

head.title: Minnesota district lookup — districtry Minnesota
head.description: Tap the map or search a Minnesota address: county, Minnesota Senate, Minnesota House and U.S. House districts — and who represents you. Free, no login.
head.og_description: Every civic district that covers a point in Minnesota, and who holds it.
head.og_image_alt: districtry Minnesota — every district that covers a point, and who represents it.
head.twitter_description: Click or search a Minnesota address to see every district that covers it.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: Congressional districts — the largest districts a state carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (congressional districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Judicial District
layers.rank_note: Ten districts of whole counties, a mean 22,000 km2 each — larger than a Senate district and smaller than a congressional one

source.answers: The judicial district covering the point: the district whose trial-court judges the reader votes on, the counties in it, the number of judgeships state law authorizes for it, and where it maintains permanent chambers.

boundary.label: Minn. Stat. 2.722 subd. 1 — the statute names the counties in each of the ten districts; the lines are those counties' own, dissolved from the county fabric this app ships, and no new boundary is drawn
Minnesota Secretary of State, voting districts — the judicial district on each of the state's 4,105 precincts, read as an independent second witness that every county sits where the statute says

source.people: NO JUDGE IS NAMED, and the reason is measured rather than assumed: www.mncourts.gov refuses all four client rungs this project has with HTTP 403 (measured 2026-10-01), so the 287 authorized judgeships have no reachable publisher here. The card states the authorized count from the statute, says plainly that it names nobody, and links the court. Gap mn-judicial-roster.

layers.label: Minnesota Senate District
layers.rank_note: 67 Senate districts, each divided into two whole House districts

source.answers: The Minnesota Senate district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (state upper chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: Not yet shipped. The card names the district and links the Minnesota Senate's own member directory; nobody is named rather than guessed. Recorded as the coverage gap mn-legislature-roster.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 87 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; this instance's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: Not yet shipped. Minnesota's 87 county boards are elected by district (447 districts), and the districts and their members arrive together in a later change; the card names no officeholder rather than guessing one. Recorded as the coverage gap mn-county-commissioner.

layers.label: Minnesota House District
layers.rank_note: 134 House districts; two nest exactly inside each Senate district, lettered A and B

source.answers: The Minnesota House district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (state lower chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app

source.people: Not yet shipped — same as the Senate above; the card links the Minnesota House's own member directory. Recorded as the coverage gap mn-legislature-roster.

layers.label: Watershed District
layers.rank_note: 64 bodies covering about 67,000 km2 of the state's 225,000 at a mean 1,050 km2 (median 316, from 20 in Richfield-Bloomington to 15,700 in Red Lake) — smaller on average than a House district and larger than a unified school district

source.answers: The watershed district or watershed management organization covering the point: what kind of body it is, the state law that creates it, who appoints its board, and its own website. Where the state's map puts the point in two, both are listed.

boundary.label: Minnesota Board of Water and Soil Resources (BWSR), Watershed Management Districts and Organizations — 45 watershed districts, 16 watershed management organizations and three county-run areas, read from the state's feature service and simplified by mn/scripts/build_mn_watershed_districts.py (Douglas-Peucker at 10 m, gated on 4,000 sampled points getting the same bodies as the source). The Geospatial Commons download host refuses this client in robots.txt and is not read

source.people: NO MANAGER IS NAMED, because no board here is elected: a watershed district's managers are appointed by the county boards of the counties it lies in (Minn. Stat. 103D.311), a metro organization's board by its member cities and towns (103B.211), and a county-run area is the county board itself. The card says who appoints the board and links the body's own website as BWSR publishes it.
source.applies: Minnesota — the parts of the state inside a watershed district or organization, 30% of its area: 99.7-99.9% of each of the seven Twin Cities counties (measured 2026-10-06 against the shipped county outlines), and wherever a district was petitioned for elsewhere.

layers.label: School District (Unified)
layers.rank_note: 322 districts covering almost all of Minnesota, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file) — 693 km2 mean feature area, the largest of the three school tilings

source.answers: The unified (every-grade) school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), queried live at runtime (no builder script, no committed data/app file); 322 features for Minnesota, measured 2026-09-29

source.people: The winners of each board's most recent elections, from the Office of the Minnesota Secretary of State's school district results files (electionresultsfiles.sos.mn.gov), dated to each election and joined to the Census district through the Minnesota Department of Education's own district layer: 1,882 of 2,099 seats on 326 boards, measured 2026-10-07. A winner is not a claim about who sits today, and the card says so; a seat a special election leaves unsettled names nobody and says why. Built weekly by mn/scripts/build_mn_school_boards.py. Gap mn-school-board-members.

layers.label: School Board District
layers.rank_note: 59 board election districts on 13 school boards, a mean 527 km2 (median 217, from 2 in Winona to 3,927 in St. Louis County) — smaller on average than a unified school district, which they divide, and larger than a commissioner district

source.answers: The election district of a school board that elects its members by district (Minn. Stat. 205A.12), and the member or members it elects. Where a precinct votes in two districts, both are named; where the results do not place a piece of a board's school district, the card says so.

boundary.label: Office of the Minnesota Secretary of State, local results by precinct (localPrct.txt) for the 2022 to 2025 generals: each district is the precincts that voted in its seat's most recent contest, read in that election's own precincts (the Secretary of State's per-general precinct layers for 2022 and 2024, today's precincts for odd years), cut to the Census school district boundary. Built by mn/scripts/build_mn_school_board_districts.py; Minneapolis's six agree with the City of Minneapolis's own park commissioner districts at all 1,800 sampled points, measured 2026-10-08
Office of the Minnesota Secretary of State, General Election Results By Precinct layers (the precincts each general was held in)

source.people: The winners of each district's most recent election, from the same school board roster the School District card reads (mn/data/app/mn-school-boards.json), every name dated. A winner is not a claim about who sits today, and the card says so.
source.applies: The 13 Minnesota school districts whose boards elect by district and whose results place those districts on precincts: Cook County, Lake Superior, Lake of the Woods, Duluth, Elk River, Winona, St. Louis County, MACCRAY, Lac qui Parle Valley, Red Rock Central, RTR, Rock Ridge and Minneapolis. Anoka-Hennepin elects by district and is not drawn (gap mn-school-board-election-districts).

layers.label: County Commissioner District
layers.rank_note: 447 districts tiling all 87 counties, 488 km2 mean feature area (median 299, from 1.8 in Ramsey to 11,154 in St. Louis) — smaller than a unified school district and larger than a ZIP code

source.answers: The county commissioner district containing the point: the seat a reader votes on for their county board, which county it belongs to, and how many commissioners that board seats.

boundary.label: Office of the Minnesota Secretary of State, Elections Division — Voting Districts, Minnesota: every one of the state's 4,105 precincts carries the commissioner district it sits in, and the districts are those precincts dissolved, so no new line is drawn. Pre-built by mn/scripts/build_mn_commissioner_districts.py.

Minn. Stat. 375.01 and 375.025 — the statute read on every run: five commissioners in every county and seven in four named ones, each county divided into as many consecutively numbered districts as it has board members. It is what makes the 447-district partition checkable rather than merely plausible.

Seven county governments' own commissioner-district layers (Anoka, Dakota, Isanti, Olmsted, Ramsey, St. Louis and Scott), read as an independent second witness: they agree with the Secretary of State about the district of every one of the 785 precincts they cover. Hennepin's and Sherburne's own layers are published on hosts whose robots.txt refuses this client, which is obeyed.

The Secretary of State's certified 2024 and 2022 general-election results, per precinct, carrying the same commissioner-district key as a dated snapshot: the 2024 table agrees with the live fabric about all 3,976 precincts they both name, and the 2022 table about 3,941 of 3,953, the twelve differences being Beltrami and Stevens redistricting after that election.

source.people: The winner of the most recent election for each seat, from the Office of the Minnesota Secretary of State's county races results files (electionresultsfiles.sos.mn.gov), dated to that election: 445 of 447 seats, the 2022 and 2024 generals plus seven special elections. A winner is not a claim about who sits today, and the card says so; five county governments' own district layers are compared each week and a disagreement (Ramsey District 3 today) is printed on the card beside the winner. Built weekly by mn/scripts/build_mn_commissioner_roster.py. Gap mn-county-commissioner-roster.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 1,385 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas intersecting Minnesota's envelope, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file) — 250 km2 mean feature area, between a school district and a township

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, queried live at runtime (no builder script, no committed data/app file). A ZCTA has NO STATE FIELD because it can cross a state line, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='27'; 1,385 features in Minnesota's envelope, measured 2026-09-29

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD SAYS SO IN AS MANY WORDS: a ZIP code elects nobody. It is a postal delivery grouping the Census approximates as an area, and the card states that rather than leaving a reader to wonder why no name appears.

layers.label: School District (Elementary)
layers.rank_note: 8 districts the Census places in its elementary tiling, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file) — 246 km2 mean feature area; they are gap-fills in the unified fabric rather than overlays on it, measured at all 8 interior points

source.answers: The elementary-tiling school district covering the point, in the eight places Minnesota has one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 2 (elementary school districts), queried live at runtime (no builder script, no committed data/app file); 8 features for Minnesota, measured 2026-09-29. SEVEN OF THE EIGHT record LOGRADE PK and HIGRADE 12, the same span as a unified district, so the card prints the recorded grades and the tiling and claims nothing about which grades the district operates — recorded as the coverage gap mn-elementary-district-grades

source.people: The same school board roster as the unified layer's row, keyed by this layer's Census district id. Gap mn-school-board-members.
source.applies: Minnesota — the eight districts the Census places in this tiling; the card is correctly empty everywhere else.

layers.label: Township or City
layers.rank_note: 2,762 records tiling the state, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file) — 1,797 townships, 901 city placeholder records for 851 distinct cities (50 of which cross a county line), 59 unorganized territories, 2 unorganized survey townships, and 3 'not defined' records that are Lake Superior water

source.answers: The organized town covering the point, or the Census placeholder record for the city that stands in place of one — and which of the two it is.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places / county subdivisions, layer 1, queried live at runtime (no builder script, no committed data/app file); 2,762 features for Minnesota, measured 2026-09-29

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER. A Minnesota town elects three supervisors to three-year terms plus a clerk and a treasurer in alternate years (Minn. Stat. 367.03, read at revisor.mn.gov on 2026-09-29), and no statewide roster of those officers was found, so the card names nobody. Recorded as the coverage gap mn-township-officers. A city's people belong on the City card and an unorganized territory's on the county's, so neither gets a town-board row at all.

layers.label: Voting Precinct
layers.rank_note: 4,105 precincts tiling the state at a 55 km2 mean feature area, pre-built from the Secretary of State's own statewide service — the finest tiling on this map, and the only layer here published by the office that maintains it rather than by the Census

source.answers: The voting precinct containing the point — where a reader votes and how their ballots are reported.

boundary.label: Office of the Minnesota Secretary of State, Elections Division — Voting Districts, Minnesota, served through MnGeo's enterprise ArcGIS host; 4,105 features, pre-built for the state by mn/scripts/build_mn_precincts.py and shipped with the app. The office states it cannot assure the lines are exact and directs anyone needing a definitive one to the city, township, or county, which the card says.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, and none is missing. A precinct elects nobody — it is an election-administration unit, not a district with a representative — so the card says that rather than leaving a reader to wonder which name is absent.

layers.label: City
layers.rank_note: 856 incorporated places, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file) — every one a city, with no village among them, at a 14.7 km2 mean feature area

source.answers: The city covering the point, if any. Most of Minnesota's land is township or unorganized territory, where the card is correctly empty.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places / incorporated places, layer 4, queried live at runtime (no builder script, no committed data/app file); 856 features for Minnesota, measured 2026-09-29, ALL of them carrying the Census's city descriptor — there is no village among them, which is why this card has no type row where Michigan's needs one

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER. A statutory city elects a mayor and council members, with a clerk and treasurer or a combined clerk-treasurer depending on its plan (Minn. Stat. 412.02, read at revisor.mn.gov on 2026-09-29); a home rule charter city's own charter governs instead. No statewide roster of Minnesota's mayors and council members was found, so the card names nobody. Recorded as the coverage gap mn-municipal-officeholders.
source.applies: Minnesota — statewide, answering only inside an incorporated city.

layers.label: School District (Secondary)
layers.rank_note: 1 district, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file) — Park Rapids for grades 9-12 over the Pine Point district, 13.3 km2, the only feature the Census publishes in this tiling for Minnesota

source.answers: The secondary school district covering the point, in the one place Minnesota has one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 1 (secondary school districts), queried live at runtime (no builder script, no committed data/app file); exactly 1 feature for Minnesota, measured 2026-09-29 — 'Park Rapids Public School District in Pine Point (9-12)'. It ships rather than being dropped because it IS the answer where it applies: without it a reader in Pine Point would be shown an elementary district and no high-school district at all

source.people: NOBODY IS NAMED HERE, deliberately: the one secondary district (Park Rapids, grades 9-12) lies over the Pine Point district, whose voters elect Pine Point's own board, so naming Park Rapids's board on this card would name people a reader there does not vote for. The Elementary card is the one for Pine Point.
source.applies: Minnesota — the single district the Census publishes in this tiling; the card is correctly empty everywhere else.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: 694 police-station points in Minnesota's envelope, live from the USGS National Map (no data/app file) — a nearest-3 proximity layer, ranked with the other point layers rather than by feature area

source.answers: The three nearest police station BUILDINGS to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through a paged loader (no builder script, no committed data/app file). Public domain. 694 points in Minnesota's envelope, measured 2026-09-29 — 448 in Minnesota and the rest in Wisconsin (200), South Dakota (24), North Dakota (15), Michigan (4) and Iowa (3), which is deliberate because nearest is a proximity fact. Name, address, city, state and ZIP are populated on every one

source.people: NOT AN OFFICEHOLDER LAYER, AND NOT A JURISDICTION EITHER. The card names buildings and says outright that which agency has jurisdiction at a point — a city police department, a county sheriff or the State Patrol — is a different question that is not published as a boundary this app can read.
source.applies: Minnesota — statewide, plus points across each border, because nearest is a proximity fact.

layers.label: Fire & EMS Station
layers.rank_note: 1,484 fire and EMS station points in Minnesota's envelope, live from the USGS National Map (no data/app file) — a nearest-3 proximity layer, ranked with the other point layers rather than by feature area

source.answers: The three nearest fire and EMS station BUILDINGS to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 51 (Fire Stations/EMS Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the same paged loader. Public domain. 1,484 points in Minnesota's envelope, measured 2026-09-29 — 961 in Minnesota, 376 in Wisconsin, 77 in South Dakota, 50 in North Dakota and 10 each in Iowa and Michigan. THE PAGING IS WHY THIS IS TRUSTWORTHY: the service caps a response and answers HTTP 200 with exceededTransferLimit rather than an error, so a truncated set looks exactly like a complete one

source.people: NOT AN OFFICEHOLDER LAYER, AND NOT A JURISDICTION EITHER. Minnesota fire protection runs on municipal departments and joint-powers contracts, so the nearest station building is not the department that would answer a call, and the card says so.
source.applies: Minnesota — statewide, plus points across each border, because nearest is a proximity fact.

layers.label: Post Office
layers.rank_note: 1,199 post-office points in Minnesota's envelope, live from the USGS National Map (no data/app file) — a nearest-3 proximity layer, so it is ranked last with the other point layers rather than by feature area

source.answers: The three nearest post offices to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 38 (Post Offices), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the same paged loader. Public domain. 1,199 points in Minnesota's envelope, measured 2026-09-29 — 793 in Minnesota, 292 in Wisconsin, 63 in South Dakota, 34 in North Dakota, 10 in Iowa and 7 in Michigan. THE SERVICE LOWERCASES THE ATTRIBUTE KEYS IT RETURNS while naming them in capitals in its own field list, which is why every read goes through the app's case-insensitive findPropCI

source.people: NOT AN OFFICEHOLDER LAYER. A post office elects nobody; the card names buildings and their addresses.
source.applies: Minnesota — statewide, plus points across each border, because nearest is a proximity fact.

negative_point.note: inside Cass County, NORTH DAKOTA, about 20 km west of Fargo — outside Minnesota and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate (minLng -97.40) so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured: 0 hits in every shipped geometry file, TIGERweb's county layer names Cass County STATE 38 (control: the anchor returns Hennepin County STATE 27), and no outline in fleet-outlines.json contains it. TWO POINTS WERE TRIED FIRST AND BOTH FAILED FOR REASONS WORTH RECORDING, because each looked obvious. LAKE SUPERIOR: Minnesota's TIGER county fabric is WATER-INCLUSIVE out to the international boundary, so a point in open Lake Superior at 47.6, -90.0 is named Lk Superior by TIGERweb's hydrography and is still INSIDE Cook County, and a point offshore of Duluth is inside the city of Duluth. Water is not outside the state here. WORTH COUNTY, IOWA (43.45, -93.37): correct on every static test — 0 hits in every shipped geometry file, TIGERweb naming Worth County STATE 19 — and it MADE THE BROWSER LEAVE. fleet-outlines.json puts it inside Iowa, so placeOwner hands the selection off to districtry.com/ia/ and the page navigates away; the smoke test's coverage-band probe then timed out looking for a button on a blank document. A NEGATIVE POINT MUST BE OUTSIDE EVERY LIVE INSTANCE, not only outside this one. Iowa's own negative point (43.65, -93.37) sits inside Minnesota and will start handing off the day this instance goes live — recorded in mn/WATCH.md as a go-live item on ia/, not a defect in this change.

geometry.note: The whole-Minnesota-state outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from all 87 counties' TIGERweb State_County layer-1 geometry by mn/scripts/build_metro_outline.py (METRO_COUNTY_FIPS = every county; DISPATCH_COUNTY_FIPS empty — no layer is county-keyed yet). Minnesota is 2-band coverage: its county tier and its statewide tier coincide, so there is no second, wider region file and coverage_key declares no region.
Every county, pre-built from TIGERweb State_County layer 1.
U.S. House districts, pre-built from TIGERweb Legislative layer 0.

The ten judicial districts, dissolved from state-counties.json by mn/scripts/build_mn_judicial_districts.py. The county membership is parsed out of Minn. Stat. 2.722 subd. 1 on every run rather than transcribed, and the write is gated three ways: the statute's lists must partition all 87 counties, the Secretary of State's judicial-district attribute on all 4,105 precincts must agree county by county, and every county's own interior anchor must land in exactly its own district.

Every watershed district and watershed management organization, from BWSR's statewide feature service by mn/scripts/build_mn_watershed_districts.py. Shipped as the state draws them, overlaps included (56 pairs touch by more than a square metre, mostly edge slivers), and gated on 2,000 statewide and 2,000 metro sample points getting the same set of bodies as the source.
Minnesota Senate districts, pre-built by mn/scripts/build_legislative_boundaries.py (2,000-point agreement gate, plus the 67-of-67 nesting gate against the House layer).
Minnesota House districts, pre-built by mn/scripts/build_legislative_boundaries.py (2,000-point agreement gate; the A/B pair of each Senate district shares its every boundary vertex).

Every county commissioner district in Minnesota, pre-built by mn/scripts/build_mn_commissioner_districts.py: the Secretary of State's 4,105 precincts dissolved on the commissioner district each one carries, so no line is drawn that a precinct boundary does not already draw. Six gates must pass before it writes — Minn. Stat. 375.01 and 375.025 read live, giving a 447-district partition of all 87 counties with consecutive numbering and a board size the statute allows; seven county governments' own layers agreeing about every one of the 785 precincts they cover; the certified 2024 and 2022 per-precinct results agreeing as dated snapshots; no point inside one district inside a second; and all 87 county anchors landing in exactly their own county's district, Cook's declared outside the fabric because it sits in Lake Superior. Simplified at a 15 m Douglas-Peucker interval over ONE shared topology, taken from the fabric's own 16.09 m median segment, so neighbouring districts share their border exactly.

Every Minnesota voting precinct, pre-built by mn/scripts/build_mn_precincts.py from the Secretary of State's own statewide service (paged at the service's 2,000-record cap; Douglas-Peucker at a 4 m interval; a 6,000-point agreement gate, measured 99.98% with zero overlaps; an exact 4,105 count floor on both the fetch and the simplified output). This instance's largest file at 1.67 MB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

Board election districts of the 13 Minnesota school boards that elect by district and whose results place them, drawn by mn/scripts/build_mn_school_board_districts.py from the Secretary of State's precinct-level results, read in each election's own precincts and cut to the Census school district. 59 districts, 4 split precincts shipped as their own features naming every district they vote in, and 5 pieces the results do not place (Duluth's combined polling places among them). Gated on the districts' precincts being disjoint, on no two features overlapping, on every seat being one the roster names, and on Minneapolis's six agreeing with the city's own park commissioner districts. Simplified at a 15 m Douglas-Peucker interval over one shared topology.

rosters.note: U.S. House roster, refreshed weekly by update-mn-congress-roster.yml.

All 447 county commissioner districts, each naming the winner of its most recent election in the Secretary of State's results and the date of that election, or saying why no name is shown; built weekly by mn/scripts/build_mn_commissioner_roster.py (update-mn-commissioner-roster.yml).

The mayor and council of each of Minnesota's 43 cities above 25,000 people, each seat naming the winner of its most recent election in the Secretary of State's city results and the date of that election, or saying why no name is shown; built weekly by mn/scripts/build_mn_city_councils.py (update-mn-city-councils.yml).

The elected board of each Minnesota school district whose elections the Secretary of State reports, keyed by the Census district id, each seat naming the winner of its most recent election and the date of that election, or saying why no name is shown; built weekly by mn/scripts/build_mn_school_boards.py (update-mn-school-boards.yml).
The Data gaps panel's content, emitted from docs/DATA_LAYER_GUIDEBOOK.md's gaps block: the county commissioner roster, the two legislature rosters, and the county officers.
